messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Unclear reserve update process",
 "problem_statement": "Users are unsure how to adjust reserves after a claim is approved, leading to delays and inaccurate financial tracking. This creates uncertainty in claim management and risks misstated liabilities.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "Could you walk me through how to update the reserves section after a claim is approved?",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-16T11:31:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The sole item is a single support quote asking how to update reserves after a claim is approved. This is a how-to question about an unclear process, likely answerable by a help article or support walkthrough, and there is no evidence of a product defect or missing functionality. No feature request, workaround, or described product flaw appears in the evidence, so this fails the help-article test.", "verdict": "fail"}
